profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.profile: This guy keeps trying to win with the irons politely holding the door while the putter sets the place on fire. The ball-striking is basically neutral to slightly annoyed, but the flat stick keeps turning decent tee-to-green work into a hostage situation. Even when the finish is good, the card usually looks like it got mugged by doubles and three-putts. The weird part is he’s still hanging around the top of the board, which means the rest of the field is also stepping on rakes. Ugly, effective, and somehow still alive.

profiles.name: Jakobm90
profiles.tagline: DRIVER GOES BANG, THE REST GETS WEIRD
profiles.profile: When this dude is on, the tee ball shows up dressed like a problem and then the rest of the bag starts asking for directions. There’s real pop off the tee, but the approach game has been a coin flip with the results tilted toward “please stop doing that.” The profile is volatile: one round looks like he might go nuclear, the next looks like he’s trying to hit greens with a blindfold and a grudge. Still, the scoring is hanging in there because the damage control has been just good enough to keep the wreck from becoming a total write-off.

profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.tagline: APPROACH SHOTS IN A WITNESS PROTECTION PROGRAM
profiles.profile: This is a full-ass mystery wrapped inside a golf swing. The tee game can absolutely hang, and the short game has enough juice to occasionally drag the corpse back to the clubhouse, but the approach numbers keep acting like the targets offended them personally. That’s why the card keeps living in the land of almost-good: enough recovery to stay relevant, enough wild misses to make you mutter into your beer. He’s basically a guy playing all the scoring shots at one speed: chaotic. If the irons ever decide to join the party, everybody else is cooked.

profiles.name: derekldavis
profiles.profile: This profile is built on survival golf with a side of demolition. The driver is not exactly a firehose, the approaches are usually late to the party, and the greens-in-regulation totals keep acting like they were negotiated down in a hostage exchange. What keeps him from fully face-planting is that he can still grind enough putts and avoid the truly catastrophic hole to turn some ugly days into merely gross. It’s not pretty, but it’s the kind of round that says, “I’m here, I hate this course, and I will outlast you by being less awful.”

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.tagline: BOOM OFF THE TEE, MAYHEM EVERYWHERE ELSE
profiles.profile: This one is all torque and turbulence. The driver can absolutely bring heat, but the rest of the round keeps showing up like a bar fight in golf shoes: a decent look here, a faceplant there, and then a parade of doubles to keep the mood honest. The short game flashes just enough to convince you there’s hope, which is rude, because the next stretch usually snatches that hope back. He can make birdies, sure, but the path there is coated in enough nonsense to qualify as performance art. Fun to watch if you don’t value your blood pressure.
